correctness.rationale: The graph is reconstructed from the standard \(G(10,3)\) edge formulas. Exact breadth-first distances give diameter 5. At scale 1, triangle-freeness and the 20-vertex, 30-edge connected graph give a wedge of 11 circles. At scale 2, exhaustive enumeration gives face vector \((20,90,120,30)\); a fully checked acyclic matching leaves one critical 0-cell and nineteen critical 2-cells. At scale 3, exhaustive enumeration gives face vector \((20,150,540,1000,960,450,80)\); a fully checked acyclic matching leaves one critical 0-cell and one critical 3-cell. At scale 4, the only forbidden pairs are the ten disjoint distance-5 antipodal pairs, so the complex is the join of ten 0-spheres, hence \(S^9\). Scale 5 is the full simplex.

value.rationale: The Desargues graph is a canonical cubic symmetric distance-transitive graph and a natural finite metric benchmark. The complete filtration is structurally informative rather than a single arbitrary number: it moves through wedge-of-circles, wedge-of-2-spheres, a 3-sphere, and a 9-sphere before contractibility. The scale-2 computation sits exactly beyond Adamaszek's girth-at-least-7 collapse criterion, so it records a meaningful boundary behavior rather than a routine recomputation.
